edges.description: Deficient TGF-beta1 signalling raises lung MMP expression, lowers elastin and retards alveolar epithelial differentiation.
The Fut8-null growth retardation is attributed to combined TGF-beta1 and EGF receptor dysfunction.
Proposed by the knockout authors as a cause of the Fut8-null growth retardation; the growth-plate or endocrine intermediate is not established.
Low integrin alpha6 levels reduce PI3K/Akt signalling in neural progenitors, and an Akt agonist rescues the neurogenic deficit.
Abnormal integrin activation is listed with the growth factor receptor defects as a cause of the knockout phenotypes.
VEGFR-2 blockade raises ceramide and alveolar septal cell apoptosis, a proposed contributor to the emphysema-like lung.
Structurally abnormal lungs are a plausible substrate for recurrent pneumonia; immune contributions have not been excluded.
Proposed link between the alveolar defect and the need for respiratory support; central hypoventilation and hypotonia may contribute.
Mouse-derived mechanism proposed for the patients' developmental delay; the human neurological mechanism is unsettled.
Fut8-deficient mice have impaired learning and memory.
Reduced neural progenitor proliferation is a plausible route to small head size, not shown directly.
The shortened limbs of the founding patients are part of the growth failure; a specific skeletal mechanism has not been studied.
Weakest link from this node; seen in one patient, and the authors suggest other genetic factors may explain it.
Polyhydramnios may reflect reduced fetal swallowing; this has not been studied.

nodes.description: The patients' features beyond growth, lung and neurogenesis (seizures, hypotonia, feeding failure, joint and spine deformity, osteopenia, glaucoma, hypothyroidism, kidney stones, facial dysmorphism) and their early mortality have no mechanism traced to a specific core-fucosylated client protein. All three founding patients died in childhood, while the four reported next were alive at 3 to 16 years.

nodes.description: Experimental. Oral L-fucose, raised to about 825 mg/kg/day with galactose added after five months, was given to one twin pair carrying a frameshift and a missense allele. Total serum N-glycan profiles did not change, but transferrin core fucosylation and some truncated glycans improved modestly, and the twins stabilised clinically, which the authors could not separate from the natural course.
